title: Set the chopsticks on their rest, never upright in the rice
instruction: serve the rice: set the chopsticks with the bowl, ready to eat
context: Chopsticks stood upright in a bowl of rice recall the incense sticks offered at funerals in Japan, China and Korea and are deeply offensive at a meal; laid across the bowl is bad manners. A robot serving food must know such norms: the right place is lying on the chopstick rest.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Bowl: the station's cream-glazed ceramic bowl, 16.6 cm across and 5.75 cm tall, fixed, centred 28 cm forward on the midline, filled with rice to about 4 cm (a fixed white disc 12.4 cm across). (2) Chopstick rest: a wooden bar 5 cm front to back, 24 cm left to right and 1 cm tall, fixed, centred 16 cm forward on the midline, just in front of the bowl. (3) Chopsticks: a pair of dark wooden chopsticks bound together with a band so they move as one, 20 cm long, 2.5 cm across and 3 cm tall overall, 30 g, loose, lying flat 15 cm forward and 17 cm right, turned 45 degrees (tips towards the far left). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. 1.0 if the chopsticks lie flat and still on the rest (their centre over the rest, their underside on its top). 0.5 if they lie flat within 15 cm of the bowl's centre but not on the rest. 0.25 if they lie across the bowl. 0.0 if they stand upright in the rice (rising more than 10 cm, centre within 9 cm of the bowl's centre) or are anywhere else, including where they started.
reset_notes: Lay the chopsticks back at their starting spot and angle. The bowl, rice and rest are fixed (putty) and stay in place.
fidelity: Dream Labs' YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The bowl is the station's own model at its scale; the rice is a thin fixed disc. The chopsticks are one rigid bar standing in for a bound pair, thicker than real ones so the gripper can hold them, and the rest is a long fixed wooden bar rather than a small hashioki.
